Keep the types whose count is strictly above the average count across trader types. Return one row with the sum of their counts, the average of their shares, and the average of (count − average count), all unrounded.

The "average amount by which counts exceed the average" is the mean of (count − avg) over the above-average types only. Same as 1, but the "average amount by which their counts exceed that average count" is the average of the absolute difference |count − average count| across the above-average types. This is the same as 1 because all of those differences are positive, so it only matters if the wording is read as a mean absolute deviation over all types.

queries:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT t.tradekind, COUNT(DISTINCT ab.translink) AS cnt
  FROM advancedbehavior ab
  JOIN transactionrecord tr ON ab.translink = tr.transreg
  JOIN trader t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg
  GROUP BY t.tradekind
),
stats AS (
  SELECT c.tradekind,
         c.cnt,
         CAST(c.cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM counts) AS share,
         (SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM counts) AS avg_cnt
  FROM counts c
)
SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count,
       AVG(share) AS avg_share,
       AVG(cnt - avg_cnt) AS avg_diff
FROM stats
WHERE cnt > avg_cnt;
SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM (SELECT t.tradekind, COUNT(a.abhvreg) AS cnt FROM trader t JOIN transactionrecord tr ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg JOIN advancedbehavior a ON a.translink = tr.transreg GROUP BY t.tradekind);
WITH c AS (
  SELECT tradekind, COUNT(*) AS trader_count
  FROM trader
  GROUP BY tradekind
)
SELECT tradekind,
       trader_count,
       (SELECT SUM(trader_count) FROM c) AS total_traders,
       (SELECT AVG(trader_count) FROM c) AS average_traders_per_type
FROM c;
SELECT tradekind, COUNT(*) AS trader_count
FROM trader
WHERE tradekind IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY tradekind;
